section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Rule of Distance
section_1.content: Establish the foundation using the Pythagorean Theorem. Explain that a sphere is simply a collection of points at a fixed distance 'R' from a center. Show the transition from 2D (x² + y² = R²) to 3D (x² + y² + z² = R²).
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'Digital Radar' device that tracks a drone. In 2D, the radar clears a circle; in 3D, it clears a bubble. As we add dimensions, we just add more 'squared' coordinates.

section_2.title: Defining the n-Sphere
section_2.content: Introduce the notation Sⁿ (the surface) and Bⁿ (the solid ball). Explain that an n-sphere exists in (n+1) dimensional space. Use a progression table to show 0-sphere (two points), 1-sphere (circle), and 2-sphere (hollow globe).
section_2.example: A 'Dimensional Traveler' character (Flatland-style) moving from a 1D line to a 3D space, showing how the 'shape' grows a new axis of symmetry each time.

section_3.title: The Volume Paradox
section_3.content: Present the formula for the volume of an n-ball. Highlight the shocking behavior: as dimensions (n) increase, the volume first increases (peaking around n=5) but then rapidly tends toward zero as n approaches infinity, even if the radius remains constant.
section_3.example: Imagine a 'Magic Balloon' that you blow into higher dimensions. At 5D, it's at its largest, but by 20D, despite having the same radius, the balloon 'mathematically vanishes' because its volume becomes nearly zero.

section_4.title: The 'Spiky' Sphere: Sphere vs. Cube
section_4.content: Compare an n-sphere inscribed inside an n-cube (side length 2R). In high dimensions, the volume of the sphere becomes an insignificant fraction of the cube's volume. Explain that the 'corners' of the cube stretch much further away than the sphere's surface.
section_4.example: The 'Hedgehog in a Box' analogy: A round hedgehog (sphere) sitting inside a square box. In 2D, the hedgehog fills most of the box. In 100D, the hedgehog is a tiny speck in the center, while the box's corners look like incredibly long, thin needles stretching away.

section_5.title: Concentration of Measure
section_5.content: Introduce the concept that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin 'shell' near the surface, or near the 'equator'. This is a fundamental concept in high-dimensional probability.
section_5.example: An 'Orange' analogy: In 3D, if you peel an orange, you get a bit of skin. In 1,000D, if you peel an orange just a tiny bit, you have removed almost 99.9% of the entire fruit's mass.

section_6.title: Application: The Curse of Dimensionality
section_6.content: Connect these geometric oddities to modern Data Science and AI. Explain that 'Nearest Neighbor' searches become difficult because in high dimensions, all points are far apart and 'distance' loses its intuitive meaning.
section_6.example: A 'Robot Librarian' trying to categorize books by 1,000 different features (dimensions). Because of the sphere properties, the librarian finds that every book feels 'equally far' from every other book, making it impossible to find a 'closest' match.

section_5.title: Concentration of Measure
section_5.content: Introduce the concept that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin 'shell' near the surface, or near the 'equator'. This is a fundamental concept in high-dimensional probability.
section_5.example: An 'Orange' analogy: In 3D, if you peel an orange, you get a bit of skin. In 1,000D, if you peel an orange just a tiny bit, you have removed almost 99.9% of the entire fruit's mass.

section_6.title: Application: The Curse of Dimensionality
section_6.content: Connect these geometric oddities to modern Data Science and AI. Explain that 'Nearest Neighbor' searches become difficult because in high dimensions, all points are far apart and 'distance' loses its intuitive meaning.
section_6.example: A 'Robot Librarian' trying to categorize books by 1,000 different features (dimensions). Because of the sphere properties, the librarian finds that every book feels 'equally far' from every other book, making it impossible to find a 'closest' match.

outline.title: The 'Spiky' Sphere: Sphere vs. Cube
outline.content: Compare an n-sphere inscribed inside an n-cube (side length 2R). In high dimensions, the volume of the sphere becomes an insignificant fraction of the cube's volume. Explain that the 'corners' of the cube stretch much further away than the sphere's surface.
outline.example: The 'Hedgehog in a Box' analogy: A round hedgehog (sphere) sitting inside a square box. In 2D, the hedgehog fills most of the box. In 100D, the hedgehog is a tiny speck in the center, while the box's corners look like incredibly long, thin needles stretching away.

The sphere becomes a tiny speck in the center.
Cube corners stretch into incredibly long, thin spikes.

In 2D, the Pythagorean Theorem defines a circle.
Higher dimensions just add more squared coordinate terms.

lecture_lines: Sⁿ is the surface; Bⁿ is the solid ball.
An n-sphere lives in n+1 dimensional space.
Each new dimension adds a new axis of symmetry.

section_3.title: The Volume Paradox
lecture_lines: n-ball volume follows a very surprising pattern.
Initially, volume increases as we add dimensions.
Volume peaks around the fifth dimension.
Then, the volume rapidly drops toward zero.
In infinite dimensions, the ball's volume effectively vanishes.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: The Curse of Dimensionality", 
            [
                "High-dimensional data creates challenges for AI and search.",
                "Points become sparse and distances lose their meaning.",
                "Every data point feels equally far from all others."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a query point surrounded by data points. Highlight the 'nearest' neighbor.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_D)
        
        query_point = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(query_point, "C3")
        query_label = Text("Query", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        query_label.next_to(query_point, UP, buff=0.1)

        data_points = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["B2"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["B4"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["D2"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["D4"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["C4"]) # Nearest one
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(query_point), FadeIn(query_label))
        self.play(Create(data_points))
        
        # Highlight nearest neighbor
        nearest_line = Line(query_point.get_center(), data_points[4].get_center(), color=GREEN)
        self.play(Create(nearest_line))
        self.play(data_points[4].animate.set_color(GREEN).scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate the points moving apart. All distance arrows turn #FFFF00 and equal length.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        target_positions = ["A1", "A6", "F1", "F6", "C6"]
        
        distance_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(data_points)):
            line = Line(query_point.get_center(), data_points[i].get_center(), color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=2)
            distance_lines.add(line)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(nearest_line), FadeIn(distance_lines))
        
        # Move points and update lines
        animations = []
        for i, point in enumerate(data_points):
            # Use updater to keep lines connected
            line = distance_lines[i]
            line.add_updater(lambda l, p=point, q=query_point: l.put_start_and_end_on(q.get_center(), p.get_center()))
            animations.append(point.animate.move_to(self.grid[target_positions[i]]))
            
        self.play(*animations, run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Change lines to yellow and "equal" length appearance
        for line in distance_lines:
            line.clear_updaters()
            
        self.play(
            distance_lines.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            data_points.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Robot icon #FFFFFF appears, unable to distinguish the 'closest' book.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Build a simple robot icon
        robot_head = Square(side_length=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        robot_eye_l = Circle(radius=0.05, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.1)
        robot_eye_r = Circle(radius=0.05, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.1)
        robot_mouth = Line(LEFT*0.15, RIGHT*0.15, color=BLACK).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + DOWN*0.1)
        robot_antenna = Line(UP*0.3, UP*0.5, color=WHITE).move_to(robot_head.get_top())
        robot_icon = VGroup(robot_head, robot_eye_l, robot_eye_r, robot_mouth, robot_antenna)
        
        self.place_at_grid(robot_icon, "E5")
        
        # Robot's confusion marker
        q_mark = Text("?", color=WHITE, font_size=36).next_to(robot_icon, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        # All distances look equal
        labels = VGroup()
        for i, point in enumerate(data_points):
            dist_label = Text("d ≈ ∞", font_size=14, color="#FFFF00")
            dist_label.move_to(Line(query_point.get_center(), point.get_center()).get_center() + UP*0.2)
            labels.add(dist_label)

        self.play(FadeIn(robot_icon))
        self.play(Write(q_mark))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels))
        
        # Final emphasis on sparsity
        self.wait(2)

```

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

            "In low dimensions, the sphere fills the cube.",
            "High dimensions push the cube's corners further away.",
            "The sphere becomes a tiny speck in the center.",
            "Cube corners stretch into incredibly long, thin spikes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lines)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        offset = np.array([0.4, 0.4, 0])
        sq_back = Square(side_length=2.5, color=COLOR_CUBE, stroke_opacity=0.5).move_to(center + offset)

            FadeIn(cube_3d), FadeIn(sphere_3d),
            Transform(dist_label_2d.copy(), dist_label_3d)
        )
        self.add(dist_label_3d)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        formula_n = MathTex("R\\sqrt{n}", font_size=32, color=COLOR_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_n, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            sphere_3d.animate.scale(0.15),
            Write(formula_n)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Cube corners stretch into incredibly long, thin spikes.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Hedgehog effect
        cube_center = cube_3d.get_center()
        simulated_corners = list(sq_front.get_vertices()) + list(sq_back.get_vertices())
        
        spikes = VGroup()
        for corner in simulated_corners:

            # Extend them far out
            extended_end = cube_center + direction * 4.5 
            spikes.add(Line(cube_center, extended_end, color=COLOR_CORNER, stroke_width=1.5))

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Rule of Distance"
        lines = [
            "A sphere is points at fixed distance from center.",
            "In 2D, the Pythagorean Theorem defines a circle.",
            "Higher dimensions just add more squared coordinate terms."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_2D = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_3D = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_R = "#FFFF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_2D))
        
        # 2D Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        center_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(0, 0), color=WHITE, radius=0.05)
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(1.5, 0), color=COLOR_2D)
        radius_line = Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1.5, 0), color=COLOR_R)
        label_r = MathTex("R", color=COLOR_R, font_size=24)
        label_r.next_to(radius_line, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(center_dot))
        self.play(Create(radius_line), FadeIn(point), Write(label_r))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition lecture line focus
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2D)
        )
        
        # Tracing a circle
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COLOR_2D).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Rule of Distance
section_1.content: Establish the foundation using the Pythagorean Theorem. Explain that a sphere is simply a collection of points at a fixed distance 'R' from a center. Show the transition from 2D (x² + y² = R²) to 3D (x² + y² + z² = R²).
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'Digital Radar' device that tracks a drone. In 2D, the radar clears a circle; in 3D, it clears a bubble. As we add dimensions, we just add more 'squared' coordinates.

section_2.title: Defining the n-Sphere
section_2.content: Introduce the notation Sⁿ (the surface) and Bⁿ (the solid ball). Explain that an n-sphere exists in (n+1) dimensional space. Use a progression table to show 0-sphere (two points), 1-sphere (circle), and 2-sphere (hollow globe).
section_2.example: A 'Dimensional Traveler' character (Flatland-style) moving from a 1D line to a 3D space, showing how the 'shape' grows a new axis of symmetry each time.

section_3.title: The Volume Paradox
section_3.content: Present the formula for the volume of an n-ball. Highlight the shocking behavior: as dimensions (n) increase, the volume first increases (peaking around n=5) but then rapidly tends toward zero as n approaches infinity, even if the radius remains constant.
section_3.example: Imagine a 'Magic Balloon' that you blow into higher dimensions. At 5D, it's at its largest, but by 20D, despite having the same radius, the balloon 'mathematically vanishes' because its volume becomes nearly zero.

section_4.title: The 'Spiky' Sphere: Sphere vs. Cube
section_4.content: Compare an n-sphere inscribed inside an n-cube (side length 2R). In high dimensions, the volume of the sphere becomes an insignificant fraction of the cube's volume. Explain that the 'corners' of the cube stretch much further away than the sphere's surface.
section_4.example: The 'Hedgehog in a Box' analogy: A round hedgehog (sphere) sitting inside a square box. In 2D, the hedgehog fills most of the box. In 100D, the hedgehog is a tiny speck in the center, while the box's corners look like incredibly long, thin needles stretching away.

section_5.title: Concentration of Measure
section_5.content: Introduce the concept that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin 'shell' near the surface, or near the 'equator'. This is a fundamental concept in high-dimensional probability.
section_5.example: An 'Orange' analogy: In 3D, if you peel an orange, you get a bit of skin. In 1,000D, if you peel an orange just a tiny bit, you have removed almost 99.9% of the entire fruit's mass.

section_6.title: Application: The Curse of Dimensionality
section_6.content: Connect these geometric oddities to modern Data Science and AI. Explain that 'Nearest Neighbor' searches become difficult because in high dimensions, all points are far apart and 'distance' loses its intuitive meaning.
section_6.example: A 'Robot Librarian' trying to categorize books by 1,000 different features (dimensions). Because of the sphere properties, the librarian finds that every book feels 'equally far' from every other book, making it impossible to find a 'closest' match.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Rule of Distance"
        lines = [
            "A sphere is points at fixed distance from center.",
            "In 2D, the Pythagorean Theorem defines a circle.",
            "Higher dimensions just add more squared coordinate terms."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_2D = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_3D = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_R = "#FFFF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_2D))
        
        # 2D Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        center_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(0, 0), color=WHITE, radius=0.05)
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(1.5, 0), color=COLOR_2D)
        radius_line = Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1.5, 0), color=COLOR_R)
        label_r = MathTex("R", color=COLOR_R, font_size=24)
        label_r.next_to(radius_line, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(center_dot))
        self.play(Create(radius_line), FadeIn(point), Write(label_r))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition lecture line focus
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2D)
        )
        
        # Tracing a circle
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COLOR_2D).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Updaters for the tracing point and radius
        point.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(1.5 * np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), 1.5 * np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()))))
        radius_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.become(Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), point.get_center(), color=COLOR_R)))
        label_r.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(radius_line, UP if abs(np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())) < 0.7 else RIGHT, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(Create(circle), angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clean up updaters
        point.clear_updaters()
        radius_line.clear_updaters()
        label_r.clear_updaters()
        
        # Display 2D Formula
        formula_2d = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_2D)
        self.place_in_area(formula_2d, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_2d))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition lecture line focus
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_3D)
        )
        
        # Reveal 3rd dimension (Z-axis)
        z_axis_end = axes.c2p(0, 0) + np.array([-1.2, -1.2, 0])
        z_axis = Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), z_axis_end, color=GREY).add_tip()
        z_label = MathTex("z", color=GREY, font_size=24).next_to(z_axis_end, DOWN+LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Sphere visualization (2.5D appearance)
        sphere_fill = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COLOR_3D, fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=0).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        sphere_cross_section = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=0.8, color=COLOR_3D).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(
            Create(z_axis),
            FadeIn(z_label),
            FadeIn(sphere_fill),
            Create(sphere_cross_section),
            FadeOut(point),
            FadeOut(radius_line),
            FadeOut(label_r)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Update formula to 3D
        formula_3d = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_3D)
        self.place_in_area(formula_3d, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula_2d, formula_3d))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition to General n-Dimensions
        formula_nd = MathTex("x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \\dots + x_n^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_3D)
        self.place_in_area(formula_nd, 'A1', 'A6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula_3d, formula_nd))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight 'R' as a constant
        self.play(formula_nd.animate.set_color_by_tex("R", COLOR_R))
        
        explanation = Text("R is a constant distance", font_size=22, color=COLOR_R)
        self.place_at_grid(explanation, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(explanation))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The 'Spiky' Sphere: Sphere vs. Cube"
        lines = [
            "Inscribe an n-sphere inside an n-cube of side 2R.",
            "In low dimensions, the sphere fills the cube.",
            "High dimensions push the cube's corners further away.",
            "The sphere becomes a tiny speck in the center.",
            "Cube corners stretch into incredibly long, thin spikes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SPHERE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_CORNER = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_CUBE = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Inscribe an n-sphere inside an n-cube of side 2R.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        square = Square(side_length=3.0, color=COLOR_CUBE)
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COLOR_SPHERE)
        
        geometry_2d = VGroup(square, circle)
        self.place_in_area(geometry_2d, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # In low dimensions, the sphere fills the cube.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Lines to corners
        corners = square.get_vertices()
        center = square.get_center()
        corner_lines = VGroup(*[Line(center, corner, color=COLOR_CORNER) for corner in corners])
        
        # Labels
        side_label = MathTex("2R", font_size=24).next_to(square, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        dist_label_2d = MathTex("R\\sqrt{2}", font_size=24, color=COLOR_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label_2d, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(corner_lines))
        self.play(Write(side_label), Write(dist_label_2d))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # High dimensions push the cube's corners further away.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Simulating 3D: Perspective Cube (Isometric-ish)
        offset = np.array([0.4, 0.4, 0])
        sq_back = Square(side_length=2.5, color=COLOR_CUBE, stroke_opacity=0.5).move_to(center + offset)
        sq_front = Square(side_length=2.5, color=COLOR_CUBE).move_to(center - offset)
        
        connectors = VGroup(*[
            Line(sq_front.get_vertices()[i], sq_back.get_vertices()[i], color=COLOR_CUBE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
            for i in range(4)
        ])
        
        cube_3d = VGroup(sq_back, sq_front, connectors)
        sphere_3d = Circle(radius=1.25, color=COLOR_SPHERE).move_to(cube_3d.get_center())
        
        # Update corner distance label for 3D
        dist_label_3d = MathTex("R\\sqrt{3}", font_size=24, color=COLOR_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label_3d, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(geometry_2d), FadeOut(corner_lines), FadeOut(dist_label_2d),
            FadeIn(cube_3d), FadeIn(sphere_3d),
            Transform(dist_label_2d.copy(), dist_label_3d)
        )
        self.add(dist_label_3d)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The sphere becomes a tiny speck in the center.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # General Formula
        formula_n = MathTex("R\\sqrt{n}", font_size=32, color=COLOR_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_n, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            sphere_3d.animate.scale(0.15),
            Write(formula_n)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Cube corners stretch into incredibly long, thin spikes.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Hedgehog effect
        cube_center = cube_3d.get_center()
        simulated_corners = list(sq_front.get_vertices()) + list(sq_back.get_vertices())
        
        spikes = VGroup()
        for corner in simulated_corners:
            direction = corner - cube_center
            # Extend them far out
            extended_end = cube_center + direction * 4.5 
            spikes.add(Line(cube_center, extended_end, color=COLOR_CORNER, stroke_width=1.5))

        self.play(
            FadeOut(cube_3d),
            FadeOut(side_label),
            Create(spikes),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        # Highlight 'n'
        n_part = formula_n[0][2] 
        self.play(n_part.animate.scale(1.5).set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(n_part.animate.scale(1/1.5).set_color(COLOR_CORNER), run_time=0.5)

        self.wait(3)

        # Final Cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: The Curse of Dimensionality", 
            [
                "High-dimensional data creates challenges for AI and search.",
                "Points become sparse and distances lose their meaning.",
                "Every data point feels equally far from all others."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a query point surrounded by data points. Highlight the 'nearest' neighbor.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_D)
        
        query_point = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(query_point, "C3")
        query_label = Text("Query", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        query_label.next_to(query_point, UP, buff=0.1)

        data_points = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["B2"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["B4"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["D2"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["D4"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["C4"]) # Nearest one
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(query_point), FadeIn(query_label))
        self.play(Create(data_points))
        
        # Highlight nearest neighbor
        nearest_line = Line(query_point.get_center(), data_points[4].get_center(), color=GREEN)
        self.play(Create(nearest_line))
        self.play(data_points[4].animate.set_color(GREEN).scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate the points moving apart. All distance arrows turn #FFFF00 and equal length.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        target_positions = ["A1", "A6", "F1", "F6", "C6"]
        
        distance_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(data_points)):
            line = Line(query_point.get_center(), data_points[i].get_center(), color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=2)
            distance_lines.add(line)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(nearest_line), FadeIn(distance_lines))
        
        # Move points and update lines
        animations = []
        for i, point in enumerate(data_points):
            # Use updater to keep lines connected
            line = distance_lines[i]
            line.add_updater(lambda l, p=point, q=query_point: l.put_start_and_end_on(q.get_center(), p.get_center()))
            animations.append(point.animate.move_to(self.grid[target_positions[i]]))
            
        self.play(*animations, run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Change lines to yellow and "equal" length appearance

            line.clear_updaters()
            
        self.play(
            distance_lines.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            data_points.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=1
        )

outline.content: Establish the foundation using the Pythagorean Theorem. Explain that a sphere is simply a collection of points at a fixed distance 'R' from a center. Show the transition from 2D (x² + y² = R²) to 3D (x² + y² + z² = R²).
outline.example: Visualizing a 'Digital Radar' device that tracks a drone. In 2D, the radar clears a circle; in 3D, it clears a bubble. As we add dimensions, we just add more 'squared' coordinates.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Rule of Distance"
        lines = [
            "A sphere is points at fixed distance from center.",
            "In 2D, the Pythagorean Theorem defines a circle.",
            "Higher dimensions just add more squared coordinate terms."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_2D = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_3D = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_R = "#FFFF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_2D))
        
        # 2D Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        center_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(0, 0), color=WHITE, radius=0.05)
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(1.5, 0), color=COLOR_2D)
        radius_line = Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1.5, 0), color=COLOR_R)
        label_r = MathTex("R", color=COLOR_R, font_size=24)
        label_r.next_to(radius_line, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(center_dot))
        self.play(Create(radius_line), FadeIn(point), Write(label_r))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition lecture line focus
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2D)
        )
        
        # Tracing a circle
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COLOR_2D).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Updaters for the tracing point and radius
        point.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(1.5 * np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), 1.5 * np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()))))
        radius_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.become(Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), point.get_center(), color=COLOR_R)))
        label_r.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(radius_line, UP if abs(np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())) < 0.7 else RIGHT, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(Create(circle), angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clean up updaters
        point.clear_updaters()
        radius_line.clear_updaters()
        label_r.clear_updaters()
        
        # Display 2D Formula
        formula_2d = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_2D)
        self.place_in_area(formula_2d, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_2d))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition lecture line focus
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_3D)
        )
        
        # Reveal 3rd dimension (Z-axis)
        z_axis_end = axes.c2p(0, 0) + np.array([-1.2, -1.2, 0])
        z_axis = Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), z_axis_end, color=GREY).add_tip()
        z_label = MathTex("z", color=GREY, font_size=24).next_to(z_axis_end, DOWN+LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Sphere visualization (2.5D appearance)
        sphere_fill = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COLOR_3D, fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=0).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        sphere_cross_section = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=0.8, color=COLOR_3D).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(
            Create(z_axis),
            FadeIn(z_label),
            FadeIn(sphere_fill),
            Create(sphere_cross_section),
            FadeOut(point),
            FadeOut(radius_line),
            FadeOut(label_r)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Update formula to 3D
        formula_3d = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_3D)
        self.place_in_area(formula_3d, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula_2d, formula_3d))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition to General n-Dimensions
        formula_nd = MathTex("x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \\dots + x_n^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_3D)
        self.place_in_area(formula_nd, 'A1', 'A6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula_3d, formula_nd))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight 'R' as a constant
        self.play(formula_nd.animate.set_color_by_tex("R", COLOR_R))
        
        explanation = Text("R is a constant distance", font_size=22, color=COLOR_R)
        self.place_at_grid(explanation, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(explanation))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The 'Spiky' Sphere: Sphere vs. Cube"
        lines = [
            "Inscribe an n-sphere inside an n-cube of side 2R.",
            "In low dimensions, the sphere fills the cube.",
            "High dimensions push the cube's corners further away.",
            "The sphere becomes a tiny speck in the center.",
            "Cube corners stretch into incredibly long, thin spikes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SPHERE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_CORNER = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_CUBE = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Inscribe an n-sphere inside an n-cube of side 2R.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        square = Square(side_length=3.0, color=COLOR_CUBE)
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=COLOR_SPHERE)
        
        geometry_2d = VGroup(square, circle)
        self.place_in_area(geometry_2d, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # In low dimensions, the sphere fills the cube.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Lines to corners
        corners = square.get_vertices()
        center = square.get_center()
        corner_lines = VGroup(*[Line(center, corner, color=COLOR_CORNER) for corner in corners])
        
        # Labels
        side_label = MathTex("2R", font_size=24).next_to(square, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        dist_label_2d = MathTex("R\\sqrt{2}", font_size=24, color=COLOR_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label_2d, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(corner_lines))
        self.play(Write(side_label), Write(dist_label_2d))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # High dimensions push the cube's corners further away.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Simulating 3D: Perspective Cube (Isometric-ish)
        offset = np.array([0.4, 0.4, 0])
        sq_back = Square(side_length=2.5, color=COLOR_CUBE, stroke_opacity=0.5).move_to(center + offset)
        sq_front = Square(side_length=2.5, color=COLOR_CUBE).move_to(center - offset)
        
        connectors = VGroup(*[
            Line(sq_front.get_vertices()[i], sq_back.get_vertices()[i], color=COLOR_CUBE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
            for i in range(4)
        ])
        
        cube_3d = VGroup(sq_back, sq_front, connectors)
        sphere_3d = Circle(radius=1.25, color=COLOR_SPHERE).move_to(cube_3d.get_center())
        
        # Update corner distance label for 3D
        dist_label_3d = MathTex("R\\sqrt{3}", font_size=24, color=COLOR_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label_3d, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(geometry_2d), FadeOut(corner_lines), FadeOut(dist_label_2d),
            FadeIn(cube_3d), FadeIn(sphere_3d),
            Transform(dist_label_2d.copy(), dist_label_3d)
        )
        self.add(dist_label_3d)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The sphere becomes a tiny speck in the center.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # General Formula
        formula_n = MathTex("R\\sqrt{n}", font_size=32, color=COLOR_CORNER)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_n, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            sphere_3d.animate.scale(0.15),
            Write(formula_n)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Cube corners stretch into incredibly long, thin spikes.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Hedgehog effect
        cube_center = cube_3d.get_center()
        simulated_corners = list(sq_front.get_vertices()) + list(sq_back.get_vertices())
        
        spikes = VGroup()
        for corner in simulated_corners:
            direction = corner - cube_center
            # Extend them far out
            extended_end = cube_center + direction * 4.5 
            spikes.add(Line(cube_center, extended_end, color=COLOR_CORNER, stroke_width=1.5))

        self.play(
            FadeOut(cube_3d),
            FadeOut(side_label),
            Create(spikes),
            run_time=3
        )

        self.wait(3)

        # Final Cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: Application: The Curse of Dimensionality
outline.content: Connect these geometric oddities to modern Data Science and AI. Explain that 'Nearest Neighbor' searches become difficult because in high dimensions, all points are far apart and 'distance' loses its intuitive meaning.
outline.example: A 'Robot Librarian' trying to categorize books by 1,000 different features (dimensions). Because of the sphere properties, the librarian finds that every book feels 'equally far' from every other book, making it impossible to find a 'closest' match.

storyboard.title: Application: The Curse of Dimensionality
lecture_lines: High-dimensional data creates challenges for AI and search.
Points become sparse and distances lose their meaning.
Every data point feels equally far from all others.
animations: Scatter points in a 3D box. Place query point in center. Area B3 to E6.
Move points far from query. Distances appear nearly equal. Area B3 to E6.
All distance lines highlight in #FFFF00. Robot icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] #FFFFFF looking confused. Area D3.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: The Curse of Dimensionality", 
            [
                "High-dimensional data creates challenges for AI and search.",
                "Points become sparse and distances lose their meaning.",
                "Every data point feels equally far from all others."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a query point surrounded by data points. Highlight the 'nearest' neighbor.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_D)
        
        query_point = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(query_point, "C3")
        query_label = Text("Query", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        query_label.next_to(query_point, UP, buff=0.1)

        data_points = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["B2"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["B4"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["D2"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["D4"]),
            Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["C4"]) # Nearest one
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(query_point), FadeIn(query_label))
        self.play(Create(data_points))
        
        # Highlight nearest neighbor
        nearest_line = Line(query_point.get_center(), data_points[4].get_center(), color=GREEN)
        self.play(Create(nearest_line))
        self.play(data_points[4].animate.set_color(GREEN).scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate the points moving apart. All distance arrows turn #FFFF00 and equal length.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        target_positions = ["A1", "A6", "F1", "F6", "C6"]
        
        distance_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(data_points)):
            line = Line(query_point.get_center(), data_points[i].get_center(), color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=2)
            distance_lines.add(line)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(nearest_line), FadeIn(distance_lines))
        
        # Move points and update lines
        animations = []
        for i, point in enumerate(data_points):
            # Use updater to keep lines connected
            line = distance_lines[i]
            line.add_updater(lambda l, p=point, q=query_point: l.put_start_and_end_on(q.get_center(), p.get_center()))
            animations.append(point.animate.move_to(self.grid[target_positions[i]]))
            
        self.play(*animations, run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Change lines to yellow and "equal" length appearance
        for line in distance_lines:
            line.clear_updaters()
            
        self.play(
            distance_lines.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            data_points.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Robot icon #FFFFFF appears, unable to distinguish the 'closest' book.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Build a simple robot icon
        robot_head = Square(side_length=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        robot_eye_l = Circle(radius=0.05, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.1)
        robot_eye_r = Circle(radius=0.05, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.1)
        robot_mouth = Line(LEFT*0.15, RIGHT*0.15, color=BLACK).move_to(robot_head.get_center() + DOWN*0.1)
        robot_antenna = Line(UP*0.3, UP*0.5, color=WHITE).move_to(robot_head.get_top())
        robot_icon = VGroup(robot_head, robot_eye_l, robot_eye_r, robot_mouth, robot_antenna)
        
        self.place_at_grid(robot_icon, "E5")
        
        # Robot's confusion marker
        q_mark = Text("?", color=WHITE, font_size=36).next_to(robot_icon, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        # All distances look equal
        labels = VGroup()
        for i, point in enumerate(data_points):
            dist_label = Text("d ≈ ∞", font_size=14, color="#FFFF00")
            dist_label.move_to(Line(query_point.get_center(), point.get_center()).get_center() + UP*0.2)
            labels.add(dist_label)

        self.play(FadeIn(robot_icon))
        self.play(Write(q_mark))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels))
        
        # Final emphasis on sparsity
        self.wait(2)

outline.content: Present the formula for the volume of an n-ball. Highlight the shocking behavior: as dimensions (n) increase, the volume first increases (peaking around n=5) but then rapidly tends toward zero as n approaches infinity, even if the radius remains constant.
outline.example: Imagine a 'Magic Balloon' that you blow into higher dimensions. At 5D, it's at its largest, but by 20D, despite having the same radius, the balloon 'mathematically vanishes' because its volume becomes nearly zero.

Volume peaks around the fifth dimension.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture content for high-dimensional spheres
        title = "Volume of High-Dimensional Spheres"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Concentration of Measure",
            "- Volume near the surface",
            "- Behavior as dimension n -> infinity",
            "- The 'fuzzy' equator concept",
            "- Counter-intuitive geometry"
        ]

        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Animation sequence
        sphere_label = Text("n-Sphere Volume", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        formula = MathTex(
            "V_n(R) = \\frac{\\pi^{n/2}}{\\Gamma(\\frac{n}{2} + 1)} R^n",
            font_size=24,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)

        # Visual representation (Proxy for high-dim sphere)
        circles = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.1 * i, color=BLUE, stroke_opacity=1.0 - (i*0.1))
            for i in range(1, 10)
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(circles, "D3", scale_factor=1.5)

        # Animate elements
        self.play(Write(sphere_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula, shift=UP))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Create(circles))
        
        # Emphasize the volume concentration
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=RED, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # Conclusion of section
        conclusion = Text("Most volume is in the shell.", font_size=22, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, "E3")
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: Concentration of Measure
outline.content: Introduce the concept that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere lies in a thin 'shell' near the surface, or near the 'equator'. This is a fundamental concept in high-dimensional probability.
outline.example: An 'Orange' analogy: In 3D, if you peel an orange, you get a bit of skin. In 1,000D, if you peel an orange just a tiny bit, you have removed almost 99.9% of the entire fruit's mass.

Think of peeling a 1,000-dimensional orange.

Volume also concentrates heavily around the equator.

        for i, point in enumerate(data_points):

        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Change lines to yellow and "equal" length appearance

        self.play(
            distance_lines.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            data_points.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),

        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Robot icon #FFFFFF appears, looking confused.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Issue 24: Use Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg

        robot_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg")
        robot_icon.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(robot_icon, "F5", scale_factor=0.8)

        q_mark = Text("?", color=WHITE, font_size=36).next_to(robot_icon, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        # All distances look equal
        labels = VGroup()
        for i, point in enumerate(data_points):
            dist_label = MathTex(r"d \approx \infty", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
            # Anchor label one unit away (B012) or at midpoint

        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
